title: A request is not an observed outcome
summary: Extract a reusable state lesson from earlier interaction-design experiments.
objectives: Distinguish requested, observed and unknown outcomes.
Avoid promoting a timeout to a successful operation.

sources.title: MDN Fetch guidance
sources.basis: Fetch responses and HTTP status need explicit checking. This does not prove that an external operation completed.

sections.title: Separate intent from observation
paragraphs: An earlier interaction-design experiment distinguished selecting Join from observing participation. Preserve that distinction without restoring its service topology or old configuration.
In a synthetic model, request changes outside to pending; an observed acknowledgement changes pending to present. A timeout changes pending to unknown.

sections.title: Reconcile before retrying
paragraphs: Unknown means the outcome has not been established. Observe current state before deciding whether another request is safe.
Authentication, permission, duplicate prevention and event ordering need separate contracts. This exercise does not implement a chat provider or a secure execution service.

exercise.instruction: Run the requested-versus-observed state exercise, including timeout and reconciliation.
exercise.expected: Request is pending; timeout is unknown; only an observed event establishes present.

limitations: Historical design lesson with a new synthetic exercise; no legacy integration was executed.
Provider APIs, credentials, customer data and private source discussions are excluded.
